    Fitting's lemma and local endomorphism rings #

    For the predicate Statement.IsIndecomposable this file proves:

    • a module is indecomposable iff it is nontrivial and its only idempotent endomorphisms are 0 and 1 (isIndecomposable_iff);
    • Fitting's lemma: an endomorphism of an indecomposable module of finite length is nilpotent or invertible, so the endomorphism ring is local (IsIndecomposable.isLocalRing_end);
    • for a module that is finite-dimensional over a field k, the radical of the endomorphism ring is nilpotent, so every product of ℓ nonunits vanishes for some ℓ ≥ 1 (exists_nonunitProductsVanish). This is the hypothesis (rad End_A(P))^ℓ = 0 of Lemma 5.1, in the form FixedSummand.NonunitProductsVanish.

    The idempotent characterization and Fitting's lemma are adapted from Modules/KrullSchmidt/IndecomposableFitting.lean and Modules/KrullSchmidt/LocalEndIndecomposable.lean in multiplicative-bases-deformations at commit 7b9f39f221d8a420a1531f487a3b93ae6d26ce85 (themselves adapted from LargeIndecomposable).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
